Chapter 9: Engaging Systems and Institutions—Advocacy, Policy, and Structural Change
When we talk about transformation, it’s easy to focus on ourselves or our immediate community. But if we really want to tackle the roots of white supremacy, we need to look deeper—right into the heart of our systems and institutions.
Here’s the big idea: even though every personal action matters, they’re just one part of the picture. If we want to dismantle systemic racism, we have to go further. That means challenging the laws, policies, and everyday practices that keep inequality alive.
Imagine a river for a moment. Sure, it’s important to help anyone who’s struggling in the current. But what if we could head upstream and stop the pollution at its source? That’s what real antiracist work looks like—not just helping individuals, but changing the systems that create injustice in the first place.
So, how do you actually get involved with these bigger structures? Let’s break it down:
First, start by educating yourself about policy. Learn how certain laws and institutional habits have created—and still maintain—racial disparities. The more you know, the more powerful your voice becomes.
Next, advocate for change. That could mean supporting leaders and policies that push for equity and justice, or speaking up when you see something that isn’t right.
Don’t forget to participate in civic life. Vote in every election. Show up at community meetings. Use your voice wherever decisions are being made—because it matters.
You can also hold institutions accountable. Whether it’s your workplace, a school, or a local organization, push for transparency, fairness, and real representation.
And finally, support grassroots movements. Lift up the work of folks who are most affected by injustice, and follow their lead. Sometimes, the most meaningful change starts from the ground up.
Want some real-world examples? Maybe you join a campaign to reform local policing, advocate for fair funding in schools, or support efforts to diversify leadership in your community. These are all ways to take action that reach beyond the personal and make a real difference.
Here’s what it comes down to: systems are just groups of people, and people working together can spark incredible change. When we challenge unjust structures as a collective, we move closer to a society that’s fair and inclusive for everyone.
